bottom_line: The data support vactosertib/pembrolizumab as a plausible investigational option, but do not support describing this patient as a likely responder on the basis of stromal/TGF-beta expression. In the studied population, nonresponse was substantially more common than objective response. The patient has prior BOT/BAL exposure, an unstudied setting in this trial; an individual numerical response probability cannot be estimated reliably.

design.phase: Open-label single-arm phase Ib/IIa at five South Korean centres
design.efficacy_planning: Expansion planned for ORR 25% versus 5% historical null; approximately 30 per dose, one-sided alpha 1%, 85% power with 20% dropout allowance. Overall observed ORR did not reach 25%.
design.selection: RECIST-measurable disease, ECOG 0-1, progression after standard therapy or intolerance/ineligibility. Five CRC patients without follow-up assessment were excluded: four rapid deterioration and one early death.

all_treated_CRC_response_fraction_sensit.note: Descriptive sensitivity, not the authors' prespecified efficacy estimate.

liver_status_posthoc.interpretation: Unplanned within-arm subgroup; organ distribution is both prognostic and potentially immunologically relevant. No randomized treatment-interaction test. Historical liver metastasis is not equivalent to active liver involvement at trial baseline.

efficacy.safety: Across CRC+GC, grade >=3 treatment-related adverse events 22/120 (18.3%); one sudden death considered possibly treatment-related. No dosing recommendation follows from this review.

biomarker_analyses.name: Baseline clinical features
biomarker_analyses.analysis: Post hoc responder 13 versus nonresponder 90; benefit 16 versus nonbenefit 87. Benefit includes CR/PR or SD >=6 months.
biomarker_analyses.results: Liver involvement associated with lower response/benefit. Responder versus nonresponder median TMB 6.6 versus 6.2 mutations/Mb (P=.609); TMB available in 12/86. NLR 3.3 versus 3.1 (P=.933). KRAS, BRAF, prior anti-EGFR, age and number of sites did not show a convincing response association. Missing mutation statuses limit interpretation.
biomarker_analyses.limits: Exploratory multiple comparisons, small responder count, no robust multivariable adjustment and no control arm; absence of association is not proof of equivalence.

biomarker_analyses.name: Circulating proteins
biomarker_analyses.analysis: C1D5 change from baseline in TGFB1, PAI-1/SERPINE1, CTGF/CCN2, PDGF-AB and PDGF-BB. Doses n=15/33/27. Source-data outcome split 10 PR versus 65 nonresponders.
biomarker_analyses.results: Dose-associated PAI-1 reduction (Kruskal-Wallis P=.0009; Dunn comparisons .0420/.0005). Other analytes did not differ by dose; no significant responder/nonresponder change differences or obvious trend.
biomarker_analyses.limits: These are early pharmacodynamic changes, not validated baseline markers. Tissue SERPINE1 protein/RNA cannot be substituted for plasma PAI-1 change.
biomarker_analyses.location: Supplementary Figures 3-4, pp10-11; Source Data Suppl Fig3/4

biomarker_analyses.name: Paired tumour IHC
biomarker_analyses.analysis: Screening versus cycle 2 day 3-6 or 10-13; CD8/FOXP3 and GZMB-positive CD8/FOXP3 ratios in tumour nests and stroma.
biomarker_analyses.results: Published paired ratios increased significantly. Independent source-data join finds zero confirmed objective responders in these IHC subsets and only two durable-SD benefit cases. Among nonbenefit cases, GZMB-positive CD8/FOXP3 increased in 15/17 tumour-nest pairs and 17/18 stromal pairs.
biomarker_analyses.limits: Strong demonstration that a favourable immune pharmacodynamic shift can occur without durable clinical benefit. Ratios can change through numerator or denominator; no randomized component control. This subset cannot identify pretreatment characteristics of objective responders.
biomarker_analyses.location: Fig5; Source Data Fig5A/B/C joined to Suppl Dataset2; peer review p7 explicitly explains missing PR tissue

biomarker_analyses.name: Published paired RNA
biomarker_analyses.analysis: 12 at 200 mg BID, 16 at 300 mg BID; post-treatment versus baseline DESeq2; KEGG hsa04350.
biomarker_analyses.results: SMAD2 decreased at 300 mg BID (log2FC about -0.35, adjusted P=.0057); SMAD6 increase was not significant (adjusted P=.0753). Supplementary Fig5B selects 21 genes by difference in fold change between dose groups (absolute delta >=0.5), not necessarily 21 individually statistically significant treatment changes.
biomarker_analyses.limits: Dose/PD analysis; no published baseline responder classifier, response-probability model, validated cutoff or external validation. Higher doses were not associated with a monotonic ORR increase.
biomarker_analyses.location: Results PD; Supplementary Fig5 p12; Source Data Suppl Fig5

biomarker_analyses.name: Exploratory RNA in transparent peer review only
biomarker_analyses.analysis: Response-stratified within-patient post/pre Hallmark fgsea. 'Responders' means PR or SD >=6 months here, unlike objective response elsewhere.
biomarker_analyses.results: Benefit group showed IFN/immune-programme induction, while nonbenefit group showed MYC/metabolic/stress programmes; author states analysis excluded from final manuscript/supplementary results because limited imbalanced samples.
biomarker_analyses.limits: This is response-associated change after treatment, not a baseline predictor. The n=34 caption is different from the published n=28 dose-specific RNA population; mapping/reason is not supplied. Do not merge these denominators, equate low pretreatment IFN with inability to induce it, or treat small within-group significance as a between-group interaction.
biomarker_analyses.location: Transparent peer review pp11-15, A-Figure3 pp12-13

processed_data_boundary.available: Clinical outcomes per subject, baseline/paired IHC ratios, circulating protein changes and dose-group gene-level DESeq2 summary; all inspected computationally.
processed_data_boundary.not_available_in_workbooks: Individual pretreatment expression matrix with response labels; a baseline RNA responder model.
processed_data_boundary.baseMean_warning: DESeq2 baseMean averages size-factor-normalized counts across samples in the contrast. It is neither baseline TPM nor a case-compatible expression reference.
processed_data_boundary.raw_reads: PRJNA1337917 publicly deposited; no FASTQ downloads or requantification performed in this review.
processed_data_boundary.case_comparison_possible_now: Compare measured case features with the direction and scope of reported biomarker associations. Cannot calculate a valid responder-similarity score from aggregate dose-level changes or bulk case RNA versus compartment-specific IHC.

case_fit.feature: Archival stromal/TGF-associated RNA and selected CAF proteins
case_fit.interpretation: Supports biological plausibility for a stromal contribution. No trial showed that higher baseline TGFB/CAF expression selected vactosertib responders; high stroma may instead be prognostic or a mixture signal.
case_fit.effect_on_efficacy_assessment: Does not justify upgrading to likely efficacy.

case_fit.interpretation: Could reflect poor recruitment/priming or weak activation rather than a physical barrier. INCA33890 patients with more inflamed baseline profiles had more favourable outcomes; the archival case does not clearly match that feature. This is a different modality and exploratory association, not proof of vactosertib resistance.
case_fit.effect_on_efficacy_assessment: A reason for caution, not an exclusion criterion.

case_fit.interpretation: CD274 Caris/BostonGene percentiles 48/71 and PDCD1 60/84 are not uniformly low, but do not measure SP263 PD-L1 tumour-area positivity or PD1/TGFBR2 coexpression on the same immune cells.
case_fit.effect_on_efficacy_assessment: Cannot apply INCA TAP thresholds to these RNA ranks.

case_fit.feature: Tissue TMB about 5/4.2 mutations per Mb
case_fit.interpretation: Compatible with the vactosertib trial's low-TMB population; trial TMB did not discriminate responders. Tissue TMB is not interchangeable with INCA blood TMB >20.
case_fit.effect_on_efficacy_assessment: Neither a strong positive selector nor proof that response is impossible.

case_fit.interpretation: Vactosertib trial excluded prior ICI. It did not test restoration of sensitivity after botensilimab/balstilimab.
case_fit.effect_on_efficacy_assessment: Major external-validity limitation; cannot assign trial ORR as personal probability.

case_fit.interpretation: If contemporary clinical assessment confirms no active liver metastases, the more favourable trial subgroup is contextually closer. Historical resected liver disease alone does not determine subgroup; organ pattern remains a nonrandomized association.
case_fit.effect_on_efficacy_assessment: Conditional modest positive context, outweighed by lack of a validated predictor and prior-ICI evidence.

case_fit.interpretation: Caris biopsy and treated resection differ; BostonGene and Tempus share B4, protein B7 is a different block, liver export is selected and no current-node molecular profile exists. Smooth muscle can inflate TGF/fibroblast signatures.
case_fit.effect_on_efficacy_assessment: Limits confidence that current resistance is driven by the nominated stromal state.

recommended_report_wording: Vactosertib plus pembrolizumab has a credible mechanism and occasional durable responses in checkpoint-naive non-MSI-high CRC, but most trial participants did not respond. The patient's data do not identify a validated responder phenotype. Low immune-recruitment signalling and prior BOT/BAL exposure reduce confidence that TGF-beta blockade alone would restore immunotherapy sensitivity; no reliable individual response estimate can be made from the present data.
scope: Inference from existing case data and published/deposited trial data only. No tissue-culture, organoid, explant or drug-screen recommendation; no additional tissue consumption proposed.
